Human: Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- every header that declares a size or index type must include <cstddef> directly and spell the type std::size_t; bare size_t is forbidden
- repeat the <cstddef>/std::size_t rule in the Full API specification and in every affected header/source implementation task
- do not rely on transitive standard-library includes, and do not use an integer shift whose width equals or exceeds the left operand's width


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- every header that declares a size or index type must include <cstddef> directly and spell the type std::size_t; bare size_t is forbidden
- repeat the <cstddef>/std::size_t rule in the Full API specification and in every affected header/source implementation task
- do not rely on transitive standard-library includes, and do not use an integer shift whose width equals or exceeds the left operand's width


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Board { public: Board() noexcept; void clear() noexcept; std::uint16_t at(std::size_t r, std::size_t c) const noexcept; void set(std::size_t r, std::size_t c, std::uint16_t v) noexcept; void getRow(std::size_t r, std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& out) const noexcept; void setRow(std::size_t r, const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& in) noexcept; void getCol(std::size_t c, std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& out) const noexcept; void setCol(std::size_t c, const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& in) noexcept; bool isFull() const noexcept; bool hasEmpty() const noexcept; std::uint16_t maxTile() const noexcept; static std::size_t side() noexcept; }; Semantics: 4x4 grid with indices r,c in [0,3]. All size/index types use std::size_t (<cstddef>). Values are non-negative 16-bit (std::uint16_t) tiles; 0 means empty. Methods do not throw; callers must respect index preconditions (no bounds checking). include/Move.h: namespace Move { enum class Direction { Left, Right, Up, Down }; struct LineMoveResult { std::array<std::uint16_t,4> line; bool moved; std::uint32_t scoreGained; }; struct BoardMoveResult { bool moved; std::uint32_t scoreGained; }; LineMoveResult processLine(const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& line) noexcept; BoardMoveResult applyMove(Board& board, Direction dir) noexcept; bool hasLegalMove(const Board& board) noexcept; } Semantics: processLine applies 2048 rules deterministically to a single 4-length line: 1) slide all non-zero values left, 2) merge adjacent equal tiles exactly once per source tile from left to right by doubling the left value and zeroing the right, accumulating scoreGained as the sum of merged values (post-merge value), 3) slide again; moved is true if resulting line differs from input. applyMove transforms the entire board for the given direction by extracting/processing rows or columns with the same slide-merge-slide rule and reapplying; returns total score gained and whether any cell changed. hasLegalMove returns true if any move would change the board (either an empty cell exists or any adjacent equal tiles exist in any direction). include/Spawner.h: class Spawner { public: bool spawn(Board& board) noexcept; void initialFill(Board& board) noexcept; }; Semantics: deterministic spawning, no randomness: spawn places a single tile with value 2 into the first empty cell in row-major order; returns true if a tile was spawned, false if the board is full. initialFill clears the board and places exactly two tiles of value 2 at the first two positions in row-major order (e.g., (0,0) and (0,1)). include/Game.h: enum class GameState { Ongoing, Won, Lost }; class Game { public: Game() noexcept; void reset() noexcept; bool move(Move::Direction dir) noexcept; const Board& board() const noexcept; std::uint32_t score() const noexcept; GameState state() const noexcept; private: /* Board board_; std::uint32_t score_; GameState state_; Spawner spawner_; */ }; Semantics: Game owns its Board and Spawner and tracks a 32-bit score. reset clears game state and uses Spawner::initialFill for deterministic start. move delegates to Move::applyMove; if no tiles moved, returns false and makes no changes. If tiles moved, increments score by scoreGained, calls Spawner::spawn once, then updates state: Won if Board::maxTile() >= 2048; Lost if not Won and Move::hasLegalMove(board) == false; otherwise Ongoing. All methods are noexcept and deterministic. Board { public: Board() noexcept; void clear() noexcept; std::uint16_t at(std::size_t r, std::size_t c) const noexcept; void set(std::size_t r, std::size_t c, std::uint16_t v) noexcept; void getRow(std::size_t r, std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& out) const noexcept; void setRow(std::size_t r, const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& in) noexcept; void getCol(std::size_t c, std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& out) const noexcept; void setCol(std::size_t c, const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& in) noexcept; bool isFull() const noexcept; bool hasEmpty() const noexcept; std::uint16_t maxTile() const noexcept; static std::size_t side() noexcept; }; Semantics: 4x4 grid with indices r,c in [0,3]. All size/index types use std::size_t (<cstddef>). Values are non-negative 16-bit (std::uint16_t) tiles; 0 means empty. Methods do not throw; callers must respect index preconditions (no bounds checking). include/Move.h: namespace Move { enum class Direction { Left, Right, Up, Down }; struct LineMoveResult { std::array<std::uint16_t,4> line; bool moved; std::uint32_t scoreGained; }; struct BoardMoveResult { bool moved; std::uint32_t scoreGained; }; LineMoveResult processLine(const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& line) noexcept; BoardMoveResult applyMove(Board& board, Direction dir) noexcept; bool hasLegalMove(const Board& board) noexcept; } Semantics: processLine applies 2048 rules deterministically to a single 4-length line: 1) slide all non-zero values left, 2) merge adjacent equal tiles exactly once per source tile from left to right by doubling the left value and zeroing the right, accumulating scoreGained as the sum of merged values (post-merge value), 3) slide again; moved is true if resulting line differs from input. applyMove transforms the entire board for the given direction by extracting/processing rows or columns with the same slide-merge-slide rule and reapplying; returns total score gained and whether any cell changed. hasLegalMove returns true if any move would change the board (either an empty cell exists or any adjacent equal tiles exist in any direction). include/Spawner.h: class Spawner { public: bool spawn(Board& board) noexcept; void initialFill(Board& board) noexcept; }; Semantics: deterministic spawning, no randomness: spawn places a single tile with value 2 into the first empty cell in row-major order; returns true if a tile was spawned, false if the board is full. initialFill clears the board and places exactly two tiles of value 2 at the first two positions in row-major order (e.g., (0,0) and (0,1)). include/Game.h: enum class GameState { Ongoing, Won, Lost }; class Game { public: Game() noexcept; void reset() noexcept; bool move(Move::Direction dir) noexcept; const Board& board() const noexcept; std::uint32_t score() const noexcept; GameState state() const noexcept; private: /* Board board_; std::uint32_t score_; GameState state_; Spawner spawner_; */ }; Semantics: Game owns its Board and Spawner and tracks a 32-bit score. reset clears game state and uses Spawner::initialFill for deterministic start. move delegates to Move::applyMove; if no tiles moved, returns false and makes no changes. If tiles moved, increments score by scoreGained, calls Spawner::spawn once, then updates state: Won if Board::maxTile() >= 2048; Lost if not Won and Move::hasLegalMove(board) == false; otherwise Ongoing. All methods are noexcept and deterministic. Board { public: Board() noexcept; void clear() noexcept; std::uint16_t at(std::size_t r, std::size_t c) const noexcept; void set(std::size_t r, std::size_t c, std::uint16_t v) noexcept; void getRow(std::size_t r, std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& out) const noexcept; void setRow(std::size_t r, const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& in) noexcept; void getCol(std::size_t c, std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& out) const noexcept; void setCol(std::size_t c, const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& in) noexcept; bool isFull() const noexcept; bool hasEmpty() const noexcept; std::uint16_t maxTile() const noexcept; static std::size_t side() noexcept; }; Semantics: 4x4 grid with indices r,c in [0,3]. All size/index types use std::size_t (<cstddef>). Values are non-negative 16-bit (std::uint16_t) tiles; 0 means empty. Methods do not throw; callers must respect index preconditions (no bounds checking). include/Move.h: namespace Move { enum class Direction { Left, Right, Up, Down }; struct LineMoveResult { std::array<std::uint16_t,4> line; bool moved; std::uint32_t scoreGained; }; struct BoardMoveResult { bool moved; std::uint32_t scoreGained; }; LineMoveResult processLine(const std::array<std::uint16_t,4>& line) noexcept; BoardMoveResult applyMove(Board& board, Direction dir) noexcept; bool hasLegalMove(const Board& board) noexcept; } Semantics: processLine applies 2048 rules deterministically to a single 4-length line: 1) slide all non-zero values left, 2) merge adjacent equal tiles exactly once per source tile from left to right by doubling the left value and zeroing the right, accumulating scoreGained as the sum of merged values (post-merge value), 3) slide again; moved is true if resulting line differs from input. applyMove transforms the entire board for the given direction by extracting/processing rows or columns with the same slide-merge-slide rule and reapplying; returns total score gained and whether any cell changed. hasLegalMove returns true if any move would change the board (either an empty cell exists or any adjacent equal tiles exist in any direction). include/Spawner.h: class Spawner { public: bool spawn(Board& board) noexcept; void initialFill(Board& board) noexcept; }; Semantics: deterministic spawning, no randomness: spawn places a single tile with value 2 into the first empty cell in row-major order; returns true if a tile was spawned, false if the board is full. initialFill clears the board and places exactly two tiles of value 2 at the first two positions in row-major order (e.g., (0,0) and (0,1)). include/Game.h: enum class GameState { Ongoing, Won, Lost }; class Game { public: Game() noexcept; void reset() noexcept; bool move(Move::Direction dir) noexcept; const Board& board() const noexcept; std::uint32_t score() const noexcept; GameState state() const noexcept; private: /* Board board_; std::uint32_t score_; GameState state_; Spawner spawner_; */ }; Semantics: Game owns its Board and Spawner and tracks a 32-bit score. reset clears game state and uses Spawner::initialFill for deterministic start. move delegates to Move::applyMove; if no tiles moved, returns false and makes no changes. If tiles moved, increments score by scoreGained, calls Spawner::spawn once, then updates state: Won if Board::maxTile() >= 2048; Lost if not Won and Move::hasLegalMove(board) == false; otherwise Ongoing. All methods are noexcept and deterministic. Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- every header that declares a size or index type must include <cstddef> directly and spell the type std::size_t; bare size_t is forbidden
- repeat the <cstddef>/std::size_t rule in the Full API specification and in every affected header/source implementation task
- do not rely on transitive standard-library includes, and do not use an integer shift whose width equals or exceeds the left operand's width


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:

- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

- 4x4 board

- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning

- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- every header that declares a size or index type must include <cstddef> directly and spell the type std::size_t; bare size_t is forbidden
- repeat the <cstddef>/std::size_t rule in the Full API specification and in every affected header/source implementation task
- do not rely on transitive standard-library includes, and do not use an integer shift whose width equals or exceeds the left operand's width


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: 2048 game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- every header that declares a size or index type must include <cstddef> directly and spell the type std::size_t; bare size_t is forbidden
- repeat the <cstddef>/std::size_t rule in the Full API specification and in every affected header/source implementation task
- do not rely on transitive standard-library includes, and do not use an integer shift whose width equals or exceeds the left operand's width


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ compilation contract:
- every header that declares a size or index type must include <cstddef> directly and spell the type std::size_t; bare size_t is forbidden
- repeat the <cstddef>/std::size_t rule in the Full API specification and in every affected header/source implementation task
- do not rely on transitive standard-library includes, and do not use an integer shift whose width equals or exceeds the left operand's width


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 7 repository files
- about 33 functions or methods
- about 650 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- 4x4 board
- left right up and down moves
- single-merge-per-move rule
- score accumulation
- deterministic tile spawning
- win loss and reset states

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents
